name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
explanation: When an element receives keyboard focus, it can't be entirely hidden behind other content the page itself put there, like a sticky header, a cookie banner, or a chat widget covering it completely. Partial overlap is allowed as long as at least some part of the focused element stays visible; what's not allowed is a focused element being fully covered so a keyboard user can't see it at all. If a user opens something that then covers a focused element, that's fine as long as they can reveal the hidden focus without needing to move focus further first.
whoItAffects: Keyboard-only users need to see the element that currently has focus in order to know what they're about to interact with, especially if they intend to press Enter or another key to act on it. Sticky headers, footers, cookie consent banners, and chat widgets are common culprits for this failure, since they're deliberately positioned to stay on screen and can end up sitting directly over a focused element as a user tabs down the page, hiding it completely without the user realizing.
howToTest: Tab through the page, paying particular attention to areas near sticky headers, sticky footers, cookie banners, or floating widgets like chat bubbles. At each focus stop, check whether the focused element is at least partially visible, not fully hidden underneath one of these overlapping elements. If tabbing ever causes a focused element to disappear completely behind fixed-position content, this fails.

check.question: A page has a sticky header 100 pixels tall. As a keyboard user tabs down the page, a form field scrolls to a position where it's completely covered by that sticky header, with no part of the field visible. Does this pass SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)?
choices: Yes, because sticky headers are a common and expected UI pattern
No, because the focused element is entirely hidden by author-created content
Yes, because the field can still be interacted with even though it's not visible
It depends only on the color contrast of the sticky header
